newsitem.title: NIGERIA: China joins Nigerian housing programme.
newsitem.headline: China joins Nigerian housing programme.

text.p: Nigeria has contracted China to build thousands of homes to rescue an embattled national housing programme, the state news agency reported on Saturday.

A memorandum of understanding on the project signed in Lagos on Friday represents another major boost to bilateral ties, have warmed since January when Chinese experts began overhauling Nigerian railways in a $520 million contract.

Works minister Major-General Abdulkareem Adisa, who signed on behalf of Nigeria, said the China Civil Engineering Construction Company would be involved in executing the national housing programme but gave no details, the agency reported.
The national programme launched in 1994 promised the delivery of 121,000 housing units nationwide within three years but so far only 3,270 units have been completed.
"The agreement with the Chinese is within the framework of technical cooperation among developing countries in the spirit of south-south cooperation," Adisa said.

Nigeria turned to China last year as relations with its traditional trading partners in the West became strained over its slow pace of democratisation and the execution of nine minority rights activists for murder.
Since then several Chinese delegations have visited Nigeria.
The Chinese also won a multi-million dollar contract to dredge a port for an export processing zone in the southeast.
The rail project has so far led to the reopening of some rail lines abandoned years ago.
